title: Characterization of the Morphology of Starch Extracted from Agricultural Residue, Specifically Mango Seed
content: The waste generated by Mexico's agro-industrial sectors is staggering. For instance, the food industry produces tons of organic waste, including peels, seeds, bones, and vegetable remains, which hold significant potential for reuse in compost production, bioenergy generation (bioethanol, biodiesel), or as raw materials for other products [1]. Mango seeds, in particular, are rich in minerals and vitamins. Ramírez-Balboa et al. [2] reported high mineral content in mango seeds, including potassium (368 mg/100 g), calcium (170 mg/100 g), and magnesium (210 mg/100 g). Additionally, they contain vitamins such as K, B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, B9, and B12, as well as biopolymers like starch. Starch, composed of approximately 20% amylose and 70% amylopectin [3], is the most widely used polysaccharide in the food industry due to its abundance, versatility, low cost, and renewable nature [3], It serves as a thickening, emulsifying, and stabilizing agent and is also utilized in the production of biodegradable films and edible coatings due to its unique physicochemical and functional properties
